sections.shortTitle: Federally Administered Tribal Areas Compulsory Primary Education Regulation 2002
sections.description:
Short title and commencement

REGULATION 1 OF 2002
REGULATION 1 OF 2002
Federally Administered Tribal
Areas Compulsory Primary Education Regulation, 2002
A Regulation to provide for
compulsory primary education in the Federally Administered Tribal Areas
[Gazette of Pakistan,
Extraordinary , Part I, 2nd May, 2002]
F.No.2(3)/2002‑Pub., dated
2‑5‑2002.‑‑The following Regulation promulgated by the
President is hereby published for general information:‑‑‑
1. Short title and
commencement.‑‑(1) This Regulation may be called the Federally
Administered Tribal Areas Compulsory Primary Education Regulation, 2002.
(2) It extends to the whole of
the Federally Administered Tribal Areas.
(3) It shall come into force at
once. .

2. Definitions.‑‑In
this Regulation, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,‑‑
(a) "Agency" or
"Authority" means the Agency, or Frontier Regions Education
Authority, notified as such by the Federal Government;
(b) "child" means a
child of either sex, whose age at the beginning of the school year is not less
than five years and not more than ten years;
(c) "Government" means
the Federal Government;
(d) "parent" include a
guardian or any other person who has the custody of a child;
(e) "primary education"
means education pertaining to all or any of the classes 1 to V in school;
(f) "primary school"
means a school in which primary education is imparted; and .
(g) recognized school" means
an institution or department of a school recognized by the Government as
suitable for imparting primary education.

3. Compulsory primary
education.‑‑The parent of a child shall, except in case of
reasonable excuse, cause a child to attend a primary school until the child has
completed the primary education course.

sections.shortTitle: Federally Administered Tribal Areas Compulsory Primary Education Regulation 2002
sections.description:
Reasonable excuse for non-attendance

REGULATION 1 OF 2002
REGULATION 1 OF 2002
Federally Administered Tribal
Areas Compulsory Primary Education Regulation, 2002
A Regulation to provide for
compulsory primary education in the Federally Administered Tribal Areas
[Gazette of Pakistan,

F.No.2(3)/2002‑Pub., dated
2‑5‑2002.‑‑The following Regulation promulgated by the
President is hereby published for general information:‑‑‑
4. Reasonable excuse for non‑attendance.‑‑Reasonable
excuse for the purpose of section (3) shall include any of the following,
namely:‑‑
(a) where the prescribed
authority is satisfied that the child is incapable of attending school by
reasons of sickness or infirmity;
(b) where the child is receiving,
otherwise than in a school, instructions which, in the opinion of the authority
is sufficient; or
(c) where there is no school or
literacy centre within a distance of 1.5 kilometres according to the nearest
route from the residence of the child.

Agency or Frontier Region Education Authority

REGULATION 1 OF 2002

President is hereby published for general information:‑‑‑
5. Agency or Frontier Region
Education Authority.‑‑(1) The Government may appoint an Agency
or Frontier Region Education Authority and if so required may appoint more than
one Deputy Agency Education (Primary Education) Authority for the agency,
Frontier Region or a part thereof.
(2) A Deputy Agency Authority or
Frontier Region Education Authority shall ensure that every child required to
attend a school within his or her jurisdiction shall take such steps as may be
considered necessary or may be specified by the Federal Government,
(3) Where an Agency or Frontier
Region Education Authority is satisfied that a parent who is required to have
his child attend school has failed to do so, the Authority after giving the
parent an opportunity of being heard and after such enquiries, may pass an
order directing the parent to make the child attend school from a date
specified in the order.

6. Offence.‑‑(1)
Any parent who fails to comply with an order issued under subsection (3) of
section 5 shall on conviction by an Assistant Political Agent be punishable
with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees and with further fine which
may extend to twenty rupees for every day after the conviction for which the
failure continues.
(2) An employer of such a child
who, after receiving due warning from the Authority, continues to employ a
child whether on remuneration or otherwise, on conviction by an Assistant
Political Agent be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees
and with a. further fine which tray extend to fifty rupees for every day after
the conviction for which the non‑attendance at a school continues.
(3) No Court shall take
cognizance of any offence under this Regulation except on a complaint in
writing made by the Authority.
